question: Define an ordered quadruple of integers $(a, b, c, d)$ as interesting if $1 \le a<b<c<d \le 10$, and $a+d>b+c$. How many interesting ordered quadruples are there?
solution:
Fix the positive gap \(k=b-a\), so \(b=a+k\). The condition \(a+d>b+c\) becomes \(d-c>k\). Together with \(c>b=a+k\), this gives \(1\le a<c-k<d-2k\le10-2k\).
Thus for fixed \(k\), choose any three distinct integers from 1 through \(10-2k\). In increasing order they specify \(a,c-k,d-2k\), so they recover exactly one valid quadruple, with \(b=a+k\). There must be at least three integers to choose from, so \(10-2k\ge3\) leaves \(k=1,2,3\). The total is \(\binom{8}{3}+\binom{6}{3}+\binom{4}{3}=56+20+4=80\).
Final answer: 80
